sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent infrastructure and local AI applications dominate today's GitHub activity. Hindsight, VoiceStudio, Paperclip, Univer, and OpenRIG point to a strong push toward persistent agent memory, autonomous work management, local voice AI, and agent-operated productivity software.

sections.title: debpalash/VoiceStudio
sections.description: Open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative for voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation.

sections.title: paperclipai/paperclip
sections.description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: Office harness for AI agents: spreadsheets, docs, slides, canvas, relational tables, and PDF.

sections.title: mvschwarz/openrig
sections.description: Multi-agent harness that runs Claude Code and Codex together as one system

sections.title: NawfalMotii79/PLFM_RADAR
sections.description: Open-source, low-cost 10.5 GHz PLFM phased-array RADAR system

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent infrastructure leads: Hindsight, Paperclip, and OpenRIG cover memory, work management, and multi-agent orchestration. VoiceStudio supplies a local multimodal AI signal. Univer extends agents into office productivity. Python leads the AI-oriented entries, while TypeScript dominates agent and productivity tooling.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: The list is shifting from standalone model demos toward operational layers around agents: memory, coordination, management, and interfaces where agents can perform office work.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's momentum is around making AI systems useful, persistent, and deployable. GitHub attention is moving up the application and infrastructure layer, especially around memory, orchestration, agent management, and local multimodal execution.
